defects.title: cholTests loads its problem file through a Windows-only relative path to a file that the repository does not ship
defects.trigger: run(matlab.unittest.TestRunner.withNoPlugins, matlab.unittest.TestSuite.fromClass(?CMatrixTest)), element CMatrixTest/cholTests, on Linux or macOS, or from any working folder without ..\..\Problem\LPnetlib\
defects.observed: MATLAB R2025a (Linux): the element is Incomplete with MATLAB:load:couldNotReadFile "Unable to find file or directory '..\..\Problem\LPnetlib\lp_80bau3b.mat'." before any assertion; the path uses backslashes (not filesep), is relative to the working folder, and no folder Problem/LPnetlib and no file lp_80bau3b.mat exists in the repository (the external sampler ships only coverage/problems/netlib/80bau3b.mat, another name and path)
defects.expected: a platform-independent path (fullfile, filesep) to a file the repository ships, or an assumption (assumeTrue) that skips the method when the file is absent

notes: DECISION 1 (quarantine reach): CMatrixTest.externalFunc lines 210-212 call sparse(1:Am, 1:Am, Carr[, Am, Am[, Am]]) with Carr = type(1:Am) a ddouble, i.e. the quarantined triplet constructor of ddouble.sparse (testDdouble.m, ddouble lines 133-136); quarantine-seeds.tsv says no src caller uses that form, which does not hold for CMatrixTest. Under III-Defects quarantine propagation the lead decides whether this row is BLOCKED instead of TESTED. Nothing in testCMatrixTest.m reaches those lines: without the MEX externalFunc stops at line 187 (type(1)), and on a machine with the MEX section 3 leaves externalFunc out, so no assertion depends on the quarantined form. DECISION 2 (severity): the cholTests defect is recorded as limitation (one of six methods depends on a problem file the repository does not ship and on a Windows path); read as 'error' it would quarantine CMatrixTest. Probe (R2025a, Linux, after initCobraToolbox): TestSuite.fromClass(?CMatrixTest) has 218 elements (comparisons 100, arithmetic 100, unaryOperations 10, externalFunc 5, otherTests 2, cholTests 1); run with TestRunner.withNoPlugins + DiagnosticsRecordingPlugin (4 s): 24 passed (comparisons with incompatible sizes return at line 37 before any type() call), 194 Incomplete: 193 MATLAB:UndefinedFunction "Undefined function 'ddoubleMex' for input arguments of type 'char'." (stack ddouble.toMex:550 -> ddouble.ddouble:26 -> CMatrixTest comparisons:40 / arithmetic:58 / unaryOperations:101 / externalFunc:187 / otherTests:222) and cholTests MATLAB:load:couldNotReadFile (defect above; runCMatrixTest.m runs from the CMatrix folder, so the path would mean sampling/Problem/LPnetlib, which does not exist). The suite has no assumeTrue on the MEX, so runCMatrixTest.m on this machine reports 194 errors and 24 vacuous passes. generateMatrices agrees with MATLAB's implicit-expansion rule (dimensions equal or 1) on all 25 x 4 parameter combinations and on sizes outside the lists, and its okay flag matches the actual broadcast sum. Run-time callees: ddouble (constructor and operators in every method but cholTests), AdaptiveChol (cholTests only); both listed. The test touches ddouble only through the Constant ddouble.mex (mexSelector -> isarm, no MEX call). A nested matlab.unittest run inside the COBRA harness (runScriptFile -> run) works and leaves nothing behind (leftover empty).

reason: No instance can be built, so no method can run: the constructor (line 70), setCholeskyTol, collapse, removeRedundantRows, rowReorder, rescale and normalize all create an AdaptiveChol, whose constructor fails at AdaptiveChol.m line 47 with "Undefined function 'AdaptiveCholMex' for input arguments of type 'uint64'." (MEX not shipped); findInterior and normalize also need analyticCenter and lewisCenter (ddoubleMex; both EXCLUDED). The documented static constructor LinearProgram, and any constructor call with the src TwoSidedBarrier, stop even earlier at line 284 with 'unsupported now' (rescale: ismethod(o.barrier, 'rescale') is false for src/analysis/sampling/BarrierRound/PolytopeSimplifier/TwoSidedBarrier.m).
notes: Probes (R2025a, after initCobraToolbox): ConvexProgram.LinearProgram([1 1 1], 1, [], zeros(3,1), ones(3,1)) -> error 'unsupported now' (ConvexProgram.rescale:284, no identifier); ConvexProgram(sparse([1 1 1]), 1, [1;1;1], [], [], TwoSidedBarrier(zeros(3,1), ones(3,1))) -> same; ConvexProgram(zeros(0,3), zeros(0,1), [], [], [], TwoSidedBarrier(zeros(3,1), ones(3,1))) (rescale returns at line 248 for an empty dimension) -> MATLAB:UndefinedFunction 'AdaptiveCholMex' at AdaptiveChol.AdaptiveChol:47 from line 70; ConvexProgram(sparse([1 1 1; 1 -1 0]), [1;0], [], [], [], <scratch handle class with only a rescale(o, s) method>) -> rescale completes (lines 248-282 run) and line 70 fails the same way. ConvexProgram.empty.rescale() -> MATLAB:minrhs, so no method can be reached without an instance. Defect lead for the lead (module-level, cannot be confirmed beyond the error because of the MEX): LinearProgram's documented inputs always end in 'unsupported now' because the shipped TwoSidedBarrier is the PolytopeSamplerMatlab version (methods set_bound, set_vdim, feasible, step_size, boundary(x) -> [A, b], gradient, hessian, tensor, quadratic_form_gradient, logdet_gradient, boundary_distance, hessian_norm) and lacks every method ConvexProgram uses: rescale (line 280), distance (88, 90), boundary(x, blocks) -> [idx, d] (100), remove (119), feasible(x) exists. The version ConvexProgram was written against is papers/2023_BarrierRound/2logBarrier/PolytopeSimplifier/TwoSidedBarrier.m (distance line 50, boundary 84, remove 97, rescale 107), not on the path. Severity if registered: error (LinearProgram cannot be called with any valid input); whether it belongs to ConvexProgram, to TwoSidedBarrier (TESTED in an earlier feature) or to the module pairing is the lead's call; logBarrierRound (wave 05) was EXCLUDED for the same chain. extra_edges: TwoSidedBarrier is constructed by LinearProgram (line 41) for every input of that static method; the six-argument constructor takes the barrier as an argument.
